comments.author: Rebar Bot Nava
comments.body:
2026-11-01 mechanism confirmed for the f3db rejection (read-only; no host change, no Gerrit change created).

Mechanism: the client's view of Gerrit main was stale, so git negated an older commit and re-sent main commits Gerrit already had, with deltas against a tree from a commit that JGit's connectivity check never marks as known.
1. 05c23655 (change 3203 ps1, parent d1a11e74) was committed 10:34:06Z. Gerrit main was 23fdf77f (merged 10:18:31Z), but this repo only fetched 23fdf77f at 10:35:32Z (refs/remotes/gerrit/main reflog). The client cannot negate an advertised tip it lacks.
2. Gerrit advertised `.have` lines for the shared account's open changes; change 3202 (ps1 745304ad / ps2 a41975c8) had parent e5a7e75b and was present locally. So the client's boundary was e5a7e75b: it sent 05c2 + d1a11e74 + 8e2201dc, using e5a7e75b's trees as thin-pack bases. f3db49d9 is e5a7e75b:src/rebar.
3. JGit FullConnectivityChecker.checkObjects:196 accepts an external base only if the walk flagged it UNINTERESTING: trees of advertised haves, plus trees of boundary commits. The server boundary was d1a11e74 (05c2's parent, reachable from main). e5a7e75b is neither, and 3202's tree has a different src/rebar, so f3db stays unflagged: "Missing tree f3db49d9".
Evidence:
- Local `git pack-objects --thin` of 05c2 with ^a41975c8: 42 objects, 19 external bases; 5 are outside the modelled JGit-marked set, f3db among them. With ^23fdf77f (after fetch): 13 objects, 10 bases, all inside the marked set.
- Host error_log 10:35:19.682Z: MissingObjectException f3db from FullConnectivityChecker.checkObjects:196 (Gerrit 3.14.1).
- Host pack-18f26c66 (10:35Z, left over from the rejected push) holds 61 objects = 42 sent + 19 bases appended by JGit, including 05c2, d1a11e74, 8e2201dc, and f3db itself. JGit read f3db to complete the thin pack, then rejected it as unreachable. pack-e51c399b (10:36Z, the accepted retry) holds 23 = 13 + 10.
- `--no-thin` is a no-op over HTTPS: GIT_TRACE of `git push --dry-run --no-thin gerrit` shows `git send-pack --stateless-rpc ... --thin`. The 10:36Z retry succeeded because of the 10:35:32Z fetch, not the flag. The Group09 failures (2 rejections with --no-thin, 2026-10-23) fit this too.
- Host (read-only): f3db, 37cf, 490430 all readable. fsck --connectivity-only rc=0 (62 unreachable commits, 71 unreachable trees, 1 unreachable blob). No alternates, no incoming/tmp packs. 363 packs, garbage 0, receive.autogc=false, receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable unset (default true). SSM afad9072-6933-48fa-aef0-c0c792c81fac, 5fb6e6e5-3d99-427a-ba76-463d365e109f.
- A delta-free pack (`-c pack.window=0 -c pack.depth=0`) of the failing case has 0 external bases.
Consequence: this is not object-store damage. infra/runbooks/gerrit-object-store-repair.md's snapshot+repair path does not apply when the named object is readable on the host. The fix choice (server knob vs client packing vs fetch-before-push) is escalated to the operator.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Review pushes to the production Gerrit (3.14.1) are intermittently rejected with `remote unpack failed: error Missing tree|blob <sha>` although the named object is readable on the host and full fsck passes. The confirmed mechanism (ticket comment of 2026-11-01): when the client's `gerrit/main` is stale, git builds a thin pack whose external delta bases come from another open change's parent; JGit `FullConnectivityChecker.checkObjects:196` accepts an external base only if its reachability walk marked it, so it rejects a readable object as missing. `git push --no-thin` is ignored over HTTPS (Git's remote-curl always runs `send-pack --thin`), so the client-side flag is not a fix. This blocks the ordinary contribution path for every session pushing from the shared bot account.

## Approach
Operator decision (2026-11-02, final): set Gerrit's `receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable = false` server-side. Gerrit documents this as a `gerrit.config` `receive.*` key (config-gerrit.html, section receive; default true); `jgit.config` holds JGit-native keys such as `receive.autogc`, so the key goes in `infra/compose/gerrit.config` under the existing `[receive]` section (`infra/compose/gerrit.config:60-62`, currently `enableSignedPush = false`), with the file's one-line `#` comment convention. With the check off, JGit still resolves thin-pack bases from the object database and still rejects objects that are truly absent; it only stops requiring that referenced objects be reachable from refs visible to the pusher. Accepted trade-off (Gerrit docs: only disable this check if clients are trusted not to forge SHA-1 references to reach commits hidden from them). Recorded basis, verbatim: "anyone who can sign in through GitHub OAuth can push for review and could read hidden commits by naming their SHA; the operator accepts this risk (2026-11-02)." Sign-in and the `refs/for/*` push ACL (`infra/gerrit/project.config:33-39`, Registered Users) stay unchanged. No client-side packing workaround is adopted.

Deploy path: `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:89` lists `infra/compose/gerrit.config` as detect-only (`config_manual`), so landing the change does not apply it. The existing operator apply (`infra/runbooks/gerrit-outbound-mail.md:62-82`) runs `infra/scripts/compose-up.sh`, whose `docker compose up -d --build` (`infra/scripts/compose-up.sh:175`) rebuilds images and would start a second MCP backend beside the live blue-green one, so it is NOT used (operator decision 2026-11-02: never run compose-up.sh for this). Instead, a narrow config-only procedure is added to that runbook section and followed: on the host, `git config -f /var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable false`; confirm no push or submit is in flight (Gerrit `show-queue`, open changes updated in the last minutes); `docker restart compose-gerrit-1` (Gerrit only; receive settings are read at startup). Back-out: `git config -f /var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config --unset receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable`, restart the Gerrit container the same way, confirm HTTP 200; no data cleanup is needed because the key changes only receive-time validation. The repo copy keeps the live file and `infra/compose/gerrit.config` in agreement for any later compose-up reseed.

## Scope
- `infra/compose/gerrit.config` — add the key with a one-line comment stating the reason and the trust trade-off.
- `tests/scripts/test_gerrit_object_store_repair.py` — pin the committed value (`git config --file ... --get receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable` == `false`).
- `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` — add the setting to the server-setting bullets beside `change.submitWholeTopic` (line 280), with the mechanism and trade-off.
- `infra/runbooks/gerrit-outbound-mail.md` — add the narrow config-only apply and back-out procedure (set key with `git config -f`, in-flight check, restart only the Gerrit container) to the "Applying a change to gerrit.config" section, and say when it is used instead of compose-up.sh.
- `infra/runbooks/gerrit-object-store-repair.md` — state that a `Missing` rejection naming an object that is readable on the host is not object-store damage and that this setting addresses it, so the snapshot+repair path is not used for it.
No repository guidance currently recommends `--no-thin` or no-delta packing (grep over docs/, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, src/rebar/_guides, infra/), so there is nothing to remove; the docs change records that `--no-thin` is not a fix.

## Testing
- New unit test pins the committed `gerrit.config` value; run `pytest tests/scripts/test_gerrit_object_store_repair.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_signals_gerrit_config.py tests/unit/test_compose_memory_limits.py`.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
- Live verification on the host after apply (see AC).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `infra/compose/gerrit.config` on merged `main` sets `receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable = false` under `[receive]` with a one-line comment; the new test asserting that value passes, and the change merged through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
- [x] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` lists the setting with its reason and the verbatim accepted trade-off; `grep -c 'could read hidden commits by naming their SHA' docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md` prints 1.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/gerrit-outbound-mail.md` documents the narrow apply and back-out procedure, and `infra/runbooks/gerrit-object-store-repair.md` distinguishes readable-object rejections from object-store damage.
- [x] The setting is applied on the production host via the narrow runbook procedure (no compose-up.sh), and `git config -f /var/gerrit/site/etc/gerrit.config --get receive.checkReferencedObjectsAreReachable` on the host prints `false` after the restart; the site answers HTTP 200.
- [x] After the apply, an ordinary `git push gerrit HEAD:refs/for/main` (no packing flags) of a review change is accepted, and the Gerrit error_log shows no new `FullConnectivityChecker` `MissingObjectException` for it.
- [x] After the apply, Gerrit-to-GitHub replication completes and `python -m rebar.mirror_guard --replication --merged-reachability --merged-limit 50` exits 0 with Gerrit and GitHub `main` equal.
- [x] The operator decision and the verbatim trade-off wording are recorded as a ticket comment.
